info.title: @mintopia/harmonic
info.description:
Queue, run, and review autonomous coding-agent tasks over ACP

## MCP

`POST /mcp` is a stateless streamable-HTTP MCP server (not a REST
endpoint, so it has no entry in this spec's paths). It authenticates the
same way as the REST API — a bearer token, either an operator API key or
the Run Key Harmonic injects into a spawned harness — and exposes the
agent task surface as MCP tools (task CRUD, dependencies, queue/cancel,
runs and events). Accept/Reject are human-only and are never exposed as
MCP tools — a verifier's pass is the accept (#140, ADR-0021). A run-scoped
Run Key may call `/mcp` regardless of the REST restrictions noted per
endpoint below. `force_integrate_epic` is an operator-only tool, the same
footing as Accept/Reject: a Run Key can call `/mcp` but gets a `forbidden`
error from it specifically — only an operator API key (`scope: 'full'`) or
an authenticated session may call it.

## WebSocket

`GET /api/ws` is a single firehose WebSocket (also outside this spec's
paths): every run event, run state change, task state change/removal, and
Conversation event/change is broadcast to every connected client as JSON
messages of the form `{ type: 'run_event' | 'run_changed' | 'run_usage' |
'task_changed' | 'task_removed' | 'conversation_event' | 'conversation_changed' |
'permission_request' | 'scheduled-jobs' | 'operations', ... }`, using the same Task/Run/Conversation/Scheduled Job/Operation shapes
served over REST. `run_usage` is a live-usage snapshot for a running Run
(tokens, context fill, derived Cost, current-activity line, and Process
Tree), pushed about once a second while the Run tails its native log.
`task_removed` (issue #162) announces a hard-deleted Task's id (`{ type:
'task_removed', id }`) — the row is gone, not another state change.
`scheduled-jobs` announces the full Scheduled Job registry snapshot, matching
`GET /api/scheduled-jobs` (ADR-0038).
`operations` announces an Operation lifecycle event, matching the operation shape
served by `GET /api/operations`.
`permission_request` announces a Harness blocked on an
operator permission decision in a Conversation (ADR-0007), answered via
`POST /conversations/:id/permissions/:reqId`. Authenticate by passing the
session token or an API key as `?token=` (WebSocket clients cannot set an
Authorization header). A `read`-scoped key gets a filtered firehose — only
`task_changed`, `task_removed`, `run_changed`, `run_event`, `run_usage`, and
`operations` — with the Conversation and permission traffic dropped.

## Read scope

A `read`-scoped API key (created via `POST /api/keys` with
`{ "scope": "read" }`) is a viz-client credential: it may `GET` tasks,
runs, maps, Operations (`/api/operations`), and the instance-wide Activity snapshot (`/api/activity`,
filtered to Runs only for a read key), and open the WebSocket (filtered as
above). Every mutation and the whole operator surface (keys, config,
channels, Conversations) is blocked. There is no `map_changed` event — a
client re-fetches `/maps` on reconnect or when it sees a `mapRef` it has
not resolved yet.

get.description: List tasks: filtered (`state`, `harness`, `priority`), searched (`q`, server-side substring over prompt + title), sorted, and paginated (`limit`/`offset`, with a `total` count). An omitted `limit` returns every match. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

schema.description: One page of tasks matching the filters, in the requested order, plus the full match `total`.

get.description: Get one task with its dependency context and Cost. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task, with its dependency context and Cost.

patch.description: Edit a draft or ready task. Each Task-default field (harness, model, isolationMode, priority) accepts null to clear it back to inherit. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The updated task.

400.description: The payload failed validation — see the error message for the offending field.

409.description: The task is running or finished, so its definition is frozen.

delete.description: Permanently delete a Task and its Runs, Usage, and Dependency edges. A mirrored Task is also dismissed so a re-poll will not re-create it. Distinct from Cancel, which keeps the record.

200.description: The id of the deleted Task.

schema.description: The id of the deleted Task.

409.description: The task is running and cannot be deleted.

post.description: Promote a draft to ready. Blocked-ness is derived from its open blockers. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task in its new state.

409.description: The task is not in a state this action can be applied to.

post.description: Cancel a non-terminal task, optionally cascading to its dependents. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task in its new state.

409.description: The task is not in a state this action can be applied to.

post.description: Force a working task to done (operator override): stop the agent and settle it done, skipping verification and merging. Operator only.

200.description: The task in its new state.

post.description: Steer a running task: send an operator message to its active run. When the harness supports ACP mid-turn steering, the message is injected into the running turn immediately — pre-empting the current generation without cancelling it. Otherwise, or when the agent is parked between turns, the message is queued and delivered as a fresh prompt turn at the next turn boundary. When no run is active but the task's last run left a still-warm, resumable session (an escalated task that ended without closure), the message continues that session in a fresh run — a follow-up in the same conversation. Use it to redirect an agent that has gone off-track, nudge one that ended its turn and parked, or continue one whose run just ended while its session is still warm. Operator only.

text.example: Stop — check the existing tests before changing the limiter.

200.description: The message was injected into the running turn or queued at the next boundary of the task's active run, or continued its last run's still-warm session in a fresh run.

409.description: The task has no active run to steer and no warm, resumable session to continue.

post.description: Return a cancelled task to the queue in place (ready; blocked-ness is derived from its open blockers). Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task in its new state.

post.description: Add a dependency edge, re-deriving the open-blocker count. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task with the edge added, and its open-blocker count re-derived.

409.description: The edge is unknown, self-referential, or would close a dependency cycle.

delete.description: Remove a dependency edge, re-deriving the open-blocker count. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The task with the edge removed, and its open-blocker count re-derived.

post.description: Accept an escalated ticket (ADR-0041): merge its verified branch head as-is and continue the success path — merge (worktree mode), close the tracker issue, clean up — moving it to done. Human-only.

200.description: The task, done.

409.description: The task is not escalated, has no verified branch head to merge, or the merging failed (the detail says why); it stays escalated.

post.description: Reject an escalated ticket with guidance (ADR-0041, amended by ADR-0048): the guidance becomes feedback for the next Attempt and the attempt budget resets. The ticket requeues to `ready` — the Auto-Runner starts the next Attempt when capacity frees; it is not force-started here unless `start: true` (the warm-Session "start now" override, which bypasses the capacity ceiling). The escalated Run's branch is retained as evidence until its Session retires. Human-only.

guidance.example: The limiter is per-process; it needs to be shared across workers.

200.description: The task, back in the Attempt loop.

post.description: Close an escalated ticket (ADR-0041): cancel it and clean up — remove its branch and worktree, close the tracker issue. Human-only.

200.description: The task, cancelled.

get.description: Preview the Session continuation a Reject with guidance will get (issue #170; decided by the #311 rule, not the operator): if this task has a live Session, the warm-session estimate and the condensed alternative. `available: false` when there is nothing to continue.

200.description: The continuation offer for this task, or `available: false`.

schema.description: The continuation offer for this task, or `available: false`.

post.description: Start an attempt for a ready task. Reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

post.description: Answer a Harness's held permission request in a Conversation (ADR-0007). `optionId` is the ACP option the operator chose — allow_once, the native allow_always ('Allow for this conversation'), or a reject option. prompt.default:
{skill}

Resolve tracker issue #{ref} ({url}) autonomously, end to end — read the issue yourself for the details. Work only on the branch you start on; Harmonic owns branching and closes the ticket once it verifies your work, so don't create branches or close the ticket yourself. When the work is done, comment a summary on the issue and call `finish_task`.

unattendedReminder.default:
## Running unattended

You are Harmonic Task {taskId} — no human is watching this turn. Ending a turn is a checkpoint, not a handoff, and Harmonic re-prompts you only a limited number of times, so don't idle-wait on background work (CI, watchers) or input. Keep working until the task is genuinely done, then call `finish_task` (taskId={taskId}). If you're blocked on a decision only a human can make, call `escalate_task` (taskId={taskId}) with a reason instead of guessing or waiting.

put.description: Full-replace the stored configuration. Unlike PATCH's deep-merge, a record key omitted here (a harness env var, a price override) is deleted, not left alone — the settings UI loads the whole config, edits locally, and saves the complete object so it can delete as well as add. Validated atomically against the config schema: an invalid body is rejected with no partial write. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

Work only on the branch you start on; Harmonic owns branching and closes the ticket once it verifies your work, so don't create branches or close the ticket yourself. When the work is done, comment a summary on the issue and call `finish_task`.

unattendedReminder.default:
## Running unattended

You are Harmonic Task {taskId} — no human is watching this turn. Ending a turn is a checkpoint, not a handoff, and Harmonic re-prompts you only a limited number of times, so don't idle-wait on background work (CI, watchers) or input. Keep working until the task is genuinely done, then call `finish_task` (taskId={taskId}). If you're blocked on a decision only a human can make, call `escalate_task` (taskId={taskId}) with a reason instead of guessing or waiting.

schema.description: The whole configuration as stored after the replace, with omitted optional fields filled from the schema's defaults.

post.description: Log in with the operator password, starting a session cookie.

200.description: The password matched; a session cookie is set on this response.

401.description: The password did not match, or no operator password has been set yet.

post.description: End the current session.

200.description: The cookie is cleared and its session destroyed; sent the same way when there was no session to end.

get.description: Whether the caller has a valid session, and whether an operator password has been set.

200.description: Whether this request's cookie names a live session, and whether an operator password is configured at all.

schema.description: Whether this request's cookie names a live session, and whether an operator password is configured at all.

post.description: Set or change the operator password. When one is already set, currentPassword must match (a wrong current password changes nothing); when none is set (ungated), currentPassword is ignored and this sets the initial password. newPassword takes the same minimum-length rule as initial setup. On success every session other than the caller's own is destroyed — a stolen cookie doesn't survive a credential rotation — but API Keys are untouched. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The password was changed; every session other than the caller's own is now destroyed, and API Keys are untouched.

400.description: newPassword is shorter than the four-character minimum, or the payload was otherwise invalid — nothing was changed.

401.description: The request carried no valid session or key, or currentPassword did not match — nothing was changed.

delete.description: Remove the operator password — Harmonic falls back to ungated (every API surface open). Verifies currentPassword first when one is set; a no-op when none is set (idempotent). On success every session other than the caller's own is destroyed. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The password is removed (or was already unset); Harmonic is now ungated.

401.description: A password is set and currentPassword did not match — nothing was changed.

post.description: Create a new operator API key. `scope` defaults to 'full' (drives the whole fleet); 'read' mints a viz-client key that can GET tasks/attempts/maps and open the WebSocket but cannot mutate anything. The bearer token is returned once and never stored.

201.description: The created key, with its bearer token in `token` — the only response that ever carries it.

schema.description: The created key, with its bearer token in `token` — the only response that ever carries it.

get.description: List operator API keys (Run Keys are internal and never listed).

200.description: Every full-scope operator key, revoked ones included, newest first; no token values.

schema.description: Every full-scope operator key, revoked ones included, newest first; no token values.

delete.description: Revoke an operator API key immediately.

200.description: The key can no longer authenticate; re-revoking an already-revoked key keeps its original revokedAt.

get.description: Usage, Cost, and run-state counts over a time range (by run start time). Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Usage, Cost, and run-state counts over the runs started in the range; totals and Cost count only what the runs actually reported and could be priced, so they are floors wherever `incomplete` is true.

schema.description: Usage, Cost, and run-state counts over the runs started in the range; totals and Cost count only what the runs actually reported and could be priced, so they are floors wherever `incomplete` is true.

get.description: Instance-wide snapshot of every capacity-consuming Run and warm Conversation across Workspaces (ADR 0010). Runs come from persisted state and join their latest live Usage, context fill, derived Cost, current-activity line, and Process Tree when available. The Activity view loads this once on page-load, then follows the live `run_usage` firehose. A Read Key (a read-scoped API key) sees Runs only — Conversations are excluded, matching the firehose filter.

200.description: Every live process across Workspaces (Runs then Conversations); an empty array when nothing is running. Unordered beyond that — the Activity view applies its own attention ranking.

schema.description: Every live process across Workspaces (Runs then Conversations); an empty array when nothing is running. Unordered beyond that — the Activity view applies its own attention ranking.

get.description: Current open Operation tree plus a bounded, in-memory history of recently completed root Operations.

200.description: The current Operation forest and recent completed root Operations.

schema.description: The current Operation forest and recent completed root Operations.

get.description: Read-only registry of recurring Harmonic Scheduled Jobs (ADR-0038), including durable last-run facts and computed next run.

200.description: The current Scheduled Job registry snapshot.

schema.description: The current Scheduled Job registry snapshot.

get.description: Read-only registry of worktrees the reconciler (ADR-0010) will not delete — dirty, unreadable, or unrecognized — awaiting operator disposition.

200.description: The current flagged-worktree registry snapshot.

schema.description: The current flagged-worktree registry snapshot.

post.description: Create a notification channel. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

201.description: The created channel; events falls back to the default subscriptions when omitted.

400.description: The payload failed validation, or the config does not match the shape the channel's type requires.

get.description: List notification channels. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Every configured notification channel.

400.description: The payload failed validation, or the config does not match the shape the channel's existing type requires.

delete.description: Delete a notification channel. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The channel was deleted, along with every per-task override pointing at it.

post.description: Add a per-task channel override: this task announces its events to this channel in addition to the channel's own subscriptions. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Every channel id now overridden for the task; adding an override that is already set changes nothing.

schema.description: Every channel id now overridden for the task; adding an override that is already set changes nothing.

get.description: List a task's per-task channel overrides. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: The channel ids overridden for the task, empty when it relies solely on the channels' own subscriptions.

schema.description: The channel ids overridden for the task, empty when it relies solely on the channels' own subscriptions.

delete.description: Remove a per-task channel override. Operator only; not reachable with a run-scoped Run Key.

200.description: Every channel id still overridden for the task; removing an override that was not set is a no-op.

schema.description: Every channel id still overridden for the task; removing an override that was not set is a no-op.

get.description: Immediate child directories of `path`, one level deep — the data behind the workspace directory picker (issue #62). An empty or omitted `path` starts at the server user's home. Files and hidden (dot) directories are excluded; entries are sorted by name. No root restriction — any directory the running user can read is browsable (a sysadmin concern, per the map decision). Operator-only: a full-scope session is required (not reachable with a scoped or read key).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Absolute path to browse; defaults to the server user home.

200.description: The browsed path, its parent, and its immediate child directories.

400.description: The path is not a directory, or the running user cannot read it.

get.description: Every derived Epic for a Workspace's last tracker poll scan (issue #167, ADR-0026), each folded with its member merge state, integration-branch tip, and whole-Epic integrate/verification state. Searched (`q`, case-insensitive substring over the Epic title) and paginated (`limit`/`offset`, with a `total`). Operator only.

200.description: Every derived Epic for this Workspace's last scan (possibly empty).

schema.description: Every derived Epic for this Workspace's last scan (possibly empty).

get.description: One derived Epic by its tracker ref, from the Workspace's last poll scan (issue #167, ADR-0026). 404s when the scan derives no leaf-most Epic with that ref. Operator only.

200.description: The derived Epic.

404.description: No Workspace has that id, or its last scan derives no Epic with that ref.

post.description: Force-integrate an Epic's ready subset: merge whatever is folded into its integration branch into the default branch now, bypassing the all-members-completed gate — but not Verification, which still gates the merge. Operator only.

200.description: The force-integrate attempt's outcome.

409.description: No active whole-Epic integrate coordinator for this Workspace (tracking is off or the loop has not started).
